cases.situation: My coworker Jen presented our joint churn analysis to the VP yesterday and kept saying 'I found' for work I did. We're peers. I want to raise it with her one on one.
cases.reply: Hey Jen, can I give you some feedback on yesterday's VP review? When you walked through the churn analysis, the cohort work I built came out as 'I found', and Marta left thinking it was all yours. I don't think you meant it that way. What's your read? For the next one, could we split the slides so each of us presents our own part?
cases.note: Observation, impact, then pause for her side before the ask; there may be context you don't have.

cases.situation: Just had a feedback conversation with my report Kevin about typos in client emails. Need the short written follow-up.
cases.reply: Thanks for the chat this afternoon, Kevin. To capture it: client emails get a read-aloud check before sending, and for the next month anything to a new client comes to me for a quick look first. Let's check in on 13 November. Tell me if I've missed anything.
cases.note: Neutral and short. The follow-up records the agreement, not the criticism.

cases.situation: Three weeks ago I told my direct report Aisha she needs to stop showing up 20 minutes late to standup. It's still happening. I want to say it firmly in our 1:1.
cases.reply: On 8 September we agreed you'd be at standup by 9:30, and you've been late four times since, including today. I need this to change now, and I'll be tracking it in our one-to-ones. What's getting in the way?
cases.note: Name the agreement and the facts, make the consequence clear, and put it in writing after. If it continues, go to HR rather than repeating the conversation.
